candidates.known_firmware_role: Unconditional 2-instruction GPIO pulse (PB30=HIGH, PB31=LOW, no restore) inside FUN_00006952.
upstream_causes: FUN_00006b50 / config_loader__CUSTOM (accepted Trigger reload) -- already known

FUN_00006e68, called only from phase_ramp_state_machine__CUSTOM's phase-3 handling -- NEW this pass: fires when an ALREADY-ARMED multi-point Auto-Mode move advances to its next programmed segment (gated on the next segment-table entry being nonzero)

FUN_00006968 (startup reference/input boot routine) -- NEW this pass: reads pin index 1 (PA22) immediately after configuring PB30/PB31 as outputs, and if HIGH at that specific boot checkpoint, calls FUN_00006952 once before the reference-seek timeout loop even starts
candidates.downstream_effects: Identical HIGH/LOW pulse every time, regardless of caller or system state. No conditional branch inside FUN_00006952 itself -- it takes no parameters and cannot vary its output.
candidates.physical_meaning: UNKNOWN. Prior pass (hardware pin map) found a plausible amber+blue SMD LED pair in the same board region as the MCU, but no copper was traced. Not re-investigated this pass (would require PCB continuity work, out of this pass's tool set).

candidates.remaining_unknown: Physical destination only (LED, another IC, external connector, or unresolved route) -- a hardware/PCB question, not a firmware-causal one. Now proven to be state-independent across 4 independent producers (not 2), which makes it a WORSE, not better, SMT target: there is no upstream ambiguity left to disambiguate.

candidates.known_firmware_role: Pulsed HIGH for ~50ms (both pins together) only inside the two byte-identical motor-driver disable sequences (FUN_000077f8 / FUN_00007868), immediately before the enable pins (PB16/PB17) are finally driven LOW.
upstream_causes: sketch_loop__CUSTOM's own motor-connector-presence poll (NEW this pass): reads a per-channel presence-detect GPIO pair for all 4 channels every main-loop iteration; when the aggregate connected/disconnected pattern changes from the previous scan, calls FUN_00007868 (if going from 'some connected' to 'none connected') or FUN_000077a0/enable (the re-detected case) -- this is the firmware side of the manual's documented 'AutoPilot auto-detects which of the four ports have a motor connected' behavior

ascii_dispatcher__CUSTOM, ASCII command 'J' (0x4A) (NEW this pass): under two mutually-exclusive sub-condition flags, reaches either FUN_00007868 or FUN_000077f8. This is a previously-undocumented wire-command link -- 'J' is not yet named/characterized elsewhere in docs/protocol/*.
candidates.downstream_effects: ~50ms HIGH pulse on PB06/PB07, then PB16/PB17 (enable) driven LOW, ending the motor-driver enable state. Re-enable (PB16/PB17 HIGH) is separately reachable from the same main-loop presence poll, from ASCII command 'J' 's counterpart path, and from inbound F0/E0 manual-jog frames (ascii_dispatcher, 0x8274/0x82d6 -- reached only when a 'was disabled' condition flag is set).
candidates.physical_meaning: Still not independently confirmed as reset vs. strobe -- this pass adds WHEN it fires (real, meaningful preconditions) but not WHAT it electrically does on the driver IC, which needs the exact driver-IC datasheet, out of reach of any tool used here.
evidence: tools/ghidra/aptrace_ghidra.py disasm autopilot868 0x8250 0x82e0 and 0x8860 0x88f0 (this session: ASCII command byte comparisons 0xF0/0xE0/'H'(0x48)/'J'(0x4A)/'&'(0x26))
docs/hardware/hardware-reference.md ('Motor presence: AutoPilot auto-detects which of the four ports have a motor connected')
candidates.remaining_unknown: Full semantics of ASCII command 'J' (not otherwise documented in docs/protocol/command-inventory.md); exact motor-presence GPIO pair sketch_loop__CUSTOM polls (not resolved this pass -- would be a new, separate signal, out of this audit's candidate list); reset-vs-strobe electrical identity.

candidates.known_firmware_role: TCC1's own IRQ handler (0x60ec, IRQ93) does an inline PORT.GROUP1.OUTTGL toggle of PB22 -- already known. This pass traces TCC1's CONFIGURATION and ENABLE/DISABLE lifecycle, previously unexamined.
upstream_causes: FUN_00005570(param_1), a per-peripheral configuration function with a switch on param_1: cases 0/1/2/3 configure TC0-TC3's own EIC/PORT setup; case 7 configures TCC1 specifically (CTRLA=0x100, a prescaler/mode write -- NOT the ENABLE bit; PER=0x20000000; CC0=0x10000). Called with values 0,1,2,3,7 (5 total calls) EXCLUSIVELY from FUN_00006968, the startup reference/input boot routine -- i.e. TCC1 is configured only once per boot, as part of the SAME sequence that also sets up the 4 real motor channels' own timers for the boot-time reference-seek move.

The only OTHER caller path into FUN_00005570 is FUN_00005f8c, itself called from FUN_00006338 (phase-2/3 monitor, x2) and ascii_dispatcher__CUSTOM (x1) -- all with per-channel arguments in the 0-3 range (motor-channel re-arm), never observed reaching case 7 in this pass's tracing. No live/wire-command path to TCC1's own configuration was found.
candidates.downstream_effects: FUN_0000434c explicitly DISABLES TCC1 (clears CTRLA bit1/ENABLE) and drives PB22 LOW, called from loop_housekeeping_save_trigger__CUSTOM's power-button-held halt sequence (and incidentally from the already-documented 'dead' ADC-baseline boot function, FUN_00005d44). This means TCC1, once configured at boot, is expected to be an ACTIVE ongoing peripheral that must be explicitly silenced on halt -- consistent with, but not proof of, it running throughout normal operation once armed.
candidates.physical_meaning: UNKNOWN which physical function PB22 drives. Functionally, the evidence points toward 'tied to the boot-time startup-reference/input sequence' (synchronization/auxiliary timing for that specific move) rather than a per-command motion channel, external control, or something unrelated to motion -- but this is an inference from co-configuration timing, not a proven functional identity.
evidence: tools/ghidra/aptrace_ghidra.py xrefs autopilot868 0x41018000 (this session: 15 references across 6 functions)
candidates.recommended_query: Starting from boot-and-hardware-bringup.md's own already-established, fully-disclosed concrete boot recipe (AUTOPILOT_RECIPE: fake-tick + the 4 clock/PLL force-bits + SERCOM clear/force-bits + PA22 seeded high + DWT stub + the radio-ID force-reg), watch 0x60ec (TCC1's IRQ handler) and the PB22 GPIO MMIO range through the SAME already-reproduced startup-reference-routine window (instructions ~27740-390000) that document's own run already covers: does TCC1's IRQ actually fire, and does PB22 actually toggle, during that window? This reuses an existing, already-validated recipe -- no new harness code needed, and it directly resolves the one remaining upstream-cause ambiguity (configuration confirmed; runtime firing not yet observed).
candidates.remaining_unknown: Whether TCC1 ever actually reaches ENABLE and fires at runtime (configuration was traced, not confirmed to result in real toggling); physical destination of PB22.
